description: German composer who expanded Classical forms with dramatic contrast, motivic development, and rhythmic drive. His piano writing is muscular, architectural, and dynamically extreme.
harmonic_language: Strong tonic-dominant polarity, dramatic deceptive cadences, sudden modulations and chromatic mediants, sforzando accents on weak beats, long dominant pedal preparations before structural arrivals.
style_notes: Build material from short, memorable motivic cells (3-4 notes) and develop them obsessively through transposition, fragmentation, and rhythmic augmentation.
Use sharp dynamic contrast: sudden ff vs p, sforzandi, crescendos that break off unexpectedly.
Accompaniment varies by character: Alberti bass or broken octaves in lyrical passages, tremolo or repeated block chords for tension, full chords for climaxes.
Sonata-form thinking: a strong first theme, a contrasting lyrical second theme in a related key, a developmental working-out, then recapitulation.
Rhythmic drive and syncopation create momentum; accents frequently fall off the beat.
Wide registral range — let the music span from deep bass octaves to the top of the keyboard for dramatic effect.
